newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters confident pensions vote will be fair.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters confident pensions vote will be fair.

text.p: New Zealand's Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Wednesday fears of a low turnout in a key referendum on compulsory superannuation due later this year were unreasonable and he rejected criticism of the vote.

"Fears of a low turnout are unfounded, but those who want a higher voter threshold on this particular issue show a lack of respect for the views of the people who have taken the trouble of examining the arguments and voting," he said in a speech.

In a prepared text of an address to an insurance company meeting, Peters defended the government's preparations of designs for a controversial private sector-led pension scheme which will be at the heart of September's vote.

He said members of parliament, among them government backbenchers, who were unhappy with accepting a majority verdict from the plebiscite and were calling for a rise in the voter threshold seemed to lack confidence in their own authority.
"Supporters of the status quo want New Zealanders to entrust future retirement income decisions to these same politicians," he said.

Peters said the designers of the proposed scheme, within the Treasury which he heads, were still working with fresh issues that were being raised. They are due to publish plans in early June to allow time for an information campaign before the vote.
"We want to see as many people as possible contributing to the debate. There are valid arguments and real fears to be addressed," he said.
